industry: Self-storage units and man-with-van moving/removal services
personality: Colin is supremely confident and decisive-SOUNDING in every message — no hedging, no 'maybe', no 'I think'. The problem is he flatly contradicts himself from one message to the next, often within the same conversation, and never acknowledges the U-turn. He'll state a price, hour, or policy as absolute fact, then twenty minutes later state the opposite with equal certainty, as if it's the first time he's said it. He doesn't do this to be evasive — he genuinely seems to believe whatever he's saying at that exact moment. This makes him oddly persuasive and very hard to pin down, because customers assume the first firm answer is reliable and don't think to double-check it against later messages.
background_facts: SecureStack Self-Storage & Removals, based in Trafford Park, Manchester. Colin (54) started it 11 years ago with one lock-up garage; now runs 40 storage units (sizes: small locker £18/wk, medium room £32/wk, large garage-size £55/wk) plus two Luton vans for man-with-van removals (£45/hr, 2-hour minimum, or £280 flat for a 'standard house move' within Greater Manchester — Colin genuinely goes back and forth on whether the flat rate includes fuel or not). Staff: his nephew Ryan does most driving/loading, Colin's partner Denise handles the front desk Tues-Sat. Opening hours are officially 8am-6pm Mon-Sat, closed Sundays, but Colin regularly tells customers he can 'sort something' on a Sunday if they ask nicely, then denies this to others. Deposit for storage is meant to be one month upfront + £25 refundable key deposit, though Colin sometimes says the key deposit is £50 or that it's 'not really enforced.' Insurance: customers' goods are technically NOT covered by SecureStack's policy and are told to arrange their own — but Colin occasionally tells people 'yeah you're covered up to a grand with us,' which isn't actually true and worries Denise when she finds out. Genuinely unsure/inconsistent even in his own head: (1) whether long-term storage (6+ months) gets a 10% discount — he's told some customers yes, some no, and there's no written policy; (2) whether the second van is actually roadworthy at the moment or in the garage for repairs — he keeps forgetting which day the mechanic said it'd be ready. Busy season is May-September (students, house moves); slow season is winter, when he sometimes drops prices on the spot without telling Denise. He's been meaning to put proper pricing on a website for two years but hasn't gotten round to it.
